sections.heading: An EC2 instance gives you control, and you patch and scale it yourself

plan.problem: A team must run code on AWS. It can rent a server, hand containers to AWS, or hand single functions to AWS. Each choice moves a different share of the work to AWS.
trace: **Rent a server.** An EC2 instance is [a virtual server in the AWS Cloud], and its instance type [determines the hardware available to your instance] (ec2-instance-virtual-server-type-sets-hardware).

**Own the operations.** You get [granular control over the compute environment], and with it the setup, scaling, patching and securing of the servers (ec2-compute-guide-ec2-overhead-justified-for-control).

**Or hand over the servers.** AWS Fargate can [run containers without having to manage servers] (ec2-compute-guide-fargate-no-servers-for-containers); AWS Lambda runs code on events [without the need to manage servers] (ec2-compute-guide-lambda-no-servers).

**Check the limits.** A Lambda function runs for at most [15 minutes] (lambda-faq-timeout-15-minutes); work with [specific resource needs or persistent processes] fits Fargate (lambda-choose-fargate-containers-persistent) or EC2.
plan.table: Who runs what (columns: Option | You manage | Fits): EC2 | the servers, the operating system and the scaling | full control of the compute environment (ec2-compute-guide-ec2-overhead-justified-for-control); Fargate | container images and task sizes | containers, long or persistent processes (lambda-choose-fargate-containers-persistent); Lambda | function code | [event-driven tasks, unpredictable workloads] (lambda-choose-functions-event-driven-unpredictable); AWS Batch | job definitions | batch jobs: it [automatically provisions compute resources] (ec2-neighbour-batch-provisions-for-jobs).
plan.why: Why offer all four? Each moves a different share of the work to AWS. The performance pillar asks you to weigh [cost (like hourly charge or data transfer)] against [management overhead (like patching and scaling)] (ec2-wa-evaluate-cost-and-management-overhead).
plan.exam_signal: "LEAST operational overhead" with "no servers to manage" points away from EC2: to Lambda for short event-driven work ([without the need to manage servers], ec2-compute-guide-lambda-no-servers), to Fargate for containers; "needs control of the operating system and installed software" points to EC2 ([granular control over the compute environment], ec2-compute-guide-ec2-overhead-justified-for-control).
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence: one workload can use [multiple types of compute solutions] (ec2-wa-multiple-compute-types-one-workload). Amazon EMR (ec2-neighbour-emr-analytics-frameworks) and AWS Elastic Beanstalk (ec2-compute-guide-beanstalk-web-apps) get one clause each at most; chapter 20 owns Batch, Beanstalk, Outposts, Local Zones and Wavelength (xref). Do not mention Lightsail (no verified fact) and do not teach EC2 managed instances (ec2-managed-instance-delegated-control is reference only).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: EC2 gives you a server to control, and you run it. The thing to watch is the work of patching and scaling it.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team converts audio files. Each conversion runs when a file arrives and takes up to 25 minutes. The team does not want to manage servers. Lambda or Fargate? Answer: Fargate (or AWS Batch); a Lambda function runs for at most [15 minutes] (lambda-faq-timeout-15-minutes). The 25 minutes are example values in the prompt; the reveal sentence carries the fact link.

sections.heading: The instance family matches the resource that limits your workload

plan.problem: Every workload runs out of one resource first: CPU, memory, local disk speed or a special processor. The family to choose is the one that has more of that resource.
trace: **Find the bottleneck.** Measure what runs out first: CPU, memory, local input and output, or work that a GPU does better.

**Pick the family.** Compute optimized fits [compute intensive applications] (ec2-family-compute-optimized); memory optimized fits workloads that [process large data sets in memory] (ec2-family-memory-optimized); storage optimized fits [very large data sets on local storage] (ec2-family-storage-optimized); accelerated computing uses [hardware accelerators, or co-processors] (ec2-family-accelerated-computing); general purpose gives [a balance of compute, memory, and networking resources] (ec2-family-general-purpose).

**Read the letter.** The first letter of the type name is the series: C [Compute optimized], M [General purpose], R [Memory optimized], I [Storage optimized], T [Burstable performance], P [GPU accelerated], G [Graphics intensive] (ec2-instance-type-series-letters).

**Pick the size.** Each type has [one or more instance sizes], so you can [scale your resources to the requirements] of the workload (ec2-instance-type-sizes-scale-resources); subsections 3 and 10 size it.
plan.table: Bottleneck to family (columns: Bottleneck | Family | Letter | Example): CPU | compute optimized | C | [batch processing workloads, media transcoding] (ec2-family-compute-optimized); memory | memory optimized | R | large data sets in memory (ec2-family-memory-optimized); local disk input and output | storage optimized | I | [low-latency, random I/O operations per second (IOPS)] (ec2-family-storage-optimized); GPU work | accelerated computing | P, G | [training of large foundation models] on P, [graphics, gaming and spatial computing] on G (ec2-faq-g-series-vs-p-series); nothing stands out | general purpose | M | [such as web servers and code repositories] (ec2-family-general-purpose).
plan.why: Why so many families? Instance types combine CPU, memory, storage and networking in different ways, and each comes in sizes that [scale your resources to the requirements] (ec2-instance-type-sizes-scale-resources), so you do not pay for a resource the workload does not use.
plan.exam_signal: "in-memory" or "large data sets in memory" points to memory optimized (ec2-family-memory-optimized); "compute-intensive", "batch processing" or "media transcoding" points to compute optimized (ec2-family-compute-optimized); "high, sequential read and write access" to local storage points to storage optimized ([high, sequential read and write access], ec2-family-storage-optimized).
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: the rest of a type name, Graviton and bare metal. After the series letter, [The second position indicates the generation] and [The third position indicates the options] (ec2-instance-type-name-structure): a means [AMD processors], g [AWS Graviton processors], d [Instance store volumes] (ec2-instance-type-option-letters). Graviton gives [up to 40% better price performance] (ec2-graviton-40-percent-better-price-performance), but compiled code must [need to be re-compiled to generate Arm binaries] (ec2-graviton-compiled-apps-recompile; rephrase so the display reads as part of the sentence). For hardware virtualization extensions, AWS suggests you [evaluate Bare Metal instances] (ec2-faq-bare-metal-for-hardware-virtualization). At most 90 words.
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence: Nitro instances [use ENA for enhanced networking] (ec2-nitro-ena-and-nvme), which gives [higher bandwidth, higher packet per second (PPS) performance] at [no additional charge for using enhanced networking] (ec2-enhanced-networking-benefits-no-charge). Do not cite Trainium and Inferentia savings unless a question needs it (ec2-faq-trainium-inferentia-save-up-to-50 is reference only). Never use the NVIDIA CUDA FAQ fact: its only display says 'we' (F2).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: pick the family by what runs out first, CPU, memory, disk or GPU. The thing to watch is the processor: Graviton needs Arm builds.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team runs an in-memory cache on a C instance. CPU use stays low, but memory runs out every afternoon. Which family letter fits better? Answer: R, memory optimized, for workloads that [process large data sets in memory] (ec2-family-memory-optimized); the C instance pays for CPU the cache does not use.

sections.heading: A burstable instance earns CPU credits while idle and spends them in peaks

plan.problem: Many servers sit almost idle and get busy for an hour or two a day. A fixed-size instance pays all day for the size of the peak.
trace: **Run at a baseline.** A T instance has a baseline CPU level and can [burst above the baseline at any time] (ec2-burstable-baseline-burst-any-time).

**Earn credits.** While it [stays below the CPU baseline], it earns CPU credits (ec2-burstable-standard-earn-spend-credits); one credit gives [a full CPU core for one minute] (ec2-burstable-cpu-credit-one-core-one-minute), and the balance holds at most the [maximum credits earned in 24 hours] (ec2-burstable-credit-accrual-limit-24-hours).
**Spend in the peak.** It [spends credits when it bursts above the baseline] (ec2-burstable-standard-earn-spend-credits).

**Run out.** In standard mode an empty balance means the [performance will remain at baseline CPU performance] (ec2-faq-t2-zero-credits-baseline, a T2 fact: keep its scope). T3 and newer types: [These instances launch as unlimited by default] (ec2-burstable-unlimited-default-t3-and-newer); the price covers spikes while the average stays at the baseline over a [rolling 24-hour period], and above it you pay a [flat additional rate per vCPU-hour] (ec2-burstable-unlimited-24-hour-baseline-rule).
plan.table: Does a T instance fit? (columns: Workload | Fits T? | Why): low average, short peaks | yes | [the low-cost burstable general purpose instances] fit low-to-moderate CPU use (ec2-burstable-low-utilization-waste-use-t); high CPU all day | no | AWS suggests you [consider dedicated CPU instances] such as M or C (ec2-faq-burstable-sustained-high-cpu-use-m-or-c); peaks longer than the saved credits, standard mode | it slows | performance falls to the baseline (ec2-faq-t2-zero-credits-baseline).
plan.why: Why credits? Most servers do not use their CPU all day; AWS says T instances can save [up to 15%] compared with M instances (ec2-burstable-t-vs-m-savings-and-smallest-size).
plan.exam_signal: "low average CPU utilization with occasional spikes" points to a burstable T instance ([the low-cost burstable general purpose instances], ec2-burstable-low-utilization-waste-use-t); "CPU utilization stays high all day" points to M or C ([consider dedicated CPU instances], ec2-faq-burstable-sustained-high-cpu-use-m-or-c).
plan.startup_example: Startup example callout, story only, at most 60 words with the label, numbers only from uses_numbers (cpu_average_percent 9, cpu_peak_percent 85): 'Callvale's demo-day instance averages 9% CPU and reaches 85% on weekday mornings. Ben moves the web tier to a burstable instance and keeps the worker on a compute optimized instance.' The story states no AWS rule; the trace above carries the facts.
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence: after a stop, T2 [the instance loses all its accrued credits], while T3 and newer keep a balance that [persists for seven days after an instance stops] (ec2-burstable-credits-after-stop-t2-lost-t3-7-days). Flex instances (ec2-faq-flex-baseline-40-burst-100) are reference only. No prices: the surplus credit rates are not taught.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: a burstable instance is cheap for a mostly idle server with short peaks. The thing to watch is a long peak, which uses up the credits.
plan.stop_and_answer: A T3 instance in unlimited mode runs at 70% CPU for 20 hours every day, far above its baseline. Does the normal hourly price cover that? Answer: no; the price covers spikes only while the average stays at the baseline over a [rolling 24-hour period], so the instance pays a [flat additional rate per vCPU-hour] (ec2-burstable-unlimited-24-hour-baseline-rule); an M or C instance fits better (ec2-faq-burstable-sustained-high-cpu-use-m-or-c). The prompt numbers are example values.

sections.heading: An AMI and a launch template let you launch identical instances

plan.problem: A server built by hand cannot be built the same way again. When it fails, or when a second copy is needed, nobody remembers every step.
trace: **Capture the image.** Create an AMI from a configured instance. By default [Amazon EC2 powers down the instance before creating the AMI] (ec2-create-ami-powers-down-by-default), and EC2 [creates snapshots of your instance's root volume] and of the other attached EBS volumes (ec2-create-ami-snapshots-all-ebs-volumes).

**Describe the launch.** A launch template stores [the AMI ID, instance type, and network settings] (ec2-launch-template-stores-launch-parameters) in numbered versions; when a launch names no version, [the default version is used] (ec2-launch-template-versions-default).

**Add first-boot work.** User data scripts [run only during the boot cycle] of the first launch by default (ec2-user-data-runs-at-first-launch-by-default), and they [run as the root user] (ec2-user-data-runs-as-root).
**Launch copies.** You can [launch multiple instances from a single AMI] (ec2-ami-specific-to-region-os-arch), all with the same software and settings.
plan.table: What an AMI keeps (columns: Part | Where it lives | In the AMI?): operating system and software | root volume | yes, as a snapshot (ec2-create-ami-snapshots-all-ebs-volumes); other EBS volumes | attached volumes | yes, as snapshots; instance store data | host disk | no: the snapshots [don't contain any data from the instance store] (ec2-create-ami-snapshots-all-ebs-volumes); user data | instance attribute | no: [user data is not included in the AMI] (ec2-user-data-not-in-ami).
plan.why: Why both an AMI and a template? The AMI fixes the software; the template fixes how an instance starts, with [the AMI ID, instance type, and network settings] (ec2-launch-template-stores-launch-parameters). Auto Scaling groups launch from the template (chapter 17, xref).
plan.exam_signal: "launch identical instances quickly" or "a golden image" points to a custom AMI and a launch template; "recover in another Region" points to copying the AMI to that Region first: [AMIs are Region-specific resources] (ec2-ami-region-specific-copy).
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence each: launch permissions decide who uses an AMI, for [specific AWS accounts, organizations, or organizational units] (ec2-ami-launch-permissions-categories), and [Some AMIs can't be made public] when they hold encrypted snapshots (ec2-ami-encrypted-cannot-be-public); AWS recommends EBS-backed AMIs because [these instances launch faster and use persistent storage] (ec2-ebs-backed-ami-recommended). Launch configurations: one xref clause to chapter 17 (ec2-auto-scaling-launch-configurations-blocked-for-new-accounts), no detail. Use a current AMI in every example: Amazon Linux 2023, not Amazon Linux 2 (ec2-change-amazon-linux-2-end-of-support-2026-06 is reference only).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: bake the software into an AMI and the settings into a launch template. The thing to watch is the Region: an AMI works only where it lives.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team creates an AMI of its database instance with the Reboot instance option cleared, so the database keeps running during the snapshot. What risk does the team accept? Answer: EC2 [it does not shut down and reboot] the instance, so AWS [can't guarantee the file system integrity] of the image (ec2-create-ami-no-reboot-integrity-risk).

sections.heading: A role gives the instance credentials, and Session Manager needs no open port

plan.problem: A server needs two kinds of access: its code calls AWS, and people log in to fix it. An access key in a file and an open SSH port are the usual shortcuts, and both leak.
trace: **Attach a role.** You attach an IAM role through an instance profile, which [can contain only one IAM role] (ec2-iam-role-one-per-instance).

**The code gets credentials.** The AWS SDKs and the AWS CLI read the role's credentials [from the EC2 instance metadata service]; [These security credentials are temporary] (ec2-iam-role-temporary-credentials-rotated) and are [temporary and updated automatically] (iam-ec2-role-credentials-rotate-automatically). Nobody copies a key: [Instead of creating and distributing your AWS credentials] (ec2-iam-role-no-credential-distribution).

**People connect.** With the managed policy [AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore] on the instance role (ec2-session-manager-prereq-iam-role), Session Manager opens a shell [without the need to open inbound ports], with no need to [maintain bastion hosts, or manage SSH keys] (ec2-session-manager-no-inbound-ports-bastion-keys).

**Close the port.** The security group keeps no inbound rule for SSH; the security pillar says [do not permit access on port 22/tcp (SSH) or port 3389/tcp (RDP)] (vpc-wa-sec06-no-ssh-rdp-use-session-manager).
plan.table: Access without keys or open ports (columns: Need | Risky way | Better way): code calls Amazon S3 | an access key in a file | an instance role, [without requiring you to manage the security credentials] (ec2-iam-role-no-credential-distribution); an admin shell | SSH on port 22 from anywhere | Session Manager, no inbound port (ec2-session-manager-no-inbound-ports-bastion-keys); an SSH or RDP client to an instance with no public IP address | a bastion host | EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, [without using a bastion host] (ec2-eice-no-public-ip-no-igw-no-bastion).
plan.why: Why temporary credentials? A copied key stays valid until someone deletes it; role credentials are [temporary and updated automatically] (iam-ec2-role-credentials-rotate-automatically). And with a key pair, AWS [doesn't keep a copy of your private key] (ec2-key-pair-private-key-not-kept): one more secret to lose.
plan.exam_signal: "without opening inbound ports" or "without managing SSH keys or a bastion host" points to Session Manager ([without the need to open inbound ports], ec2-session-manager-no-inbound-ports-bastion-keys); "an application on the instance needs access to Amazon S3" points to an IAM role for the instance (ec2-iam-role-no-credential-distribution), never to an access key stored on it.
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: IMDSv2 and the hop limit. By default an instance accepts [either IMDSv1 or IMDSv2, or both]; you can make it [only accept IMDSv2 calls] (ec2-imds-default-v1-or-v2), which use a session token. The token response has a [hop limit of 1] by default, and AWS suggests [increasing the hop limit to 2] for containers (ec2-imds-put-hop-limit-default-1). An account default can make new instances [launch with IMDSv2 required] (ec2-imds-account-default-v2-new-instances). At most 90 words.
plan.spot_the_bug: Spot the bug prompt: a user data script writes an access key ID and a secret access key into the file ~/.aws/credentials so that the application can call Amazon S3. Find the bug. Reveal: user data is [not protected by authentication or cryptographic methods] (ec2-metadata-user-data-not-protected), and the key is long-term; attach an instance role instead (ec2-iam-role-no-credential-distribution). About 65 words with the reveal.
plan.body_extras: Do not write how the SSM Agent reaches Systems Manager (outbound path, NAT gateway or interface endpoints) until fact request fr-0061 is filled. Security group detail belongs to chapter 10: one clause at most, for example that groups are [Security groups are stateful] (ec2-security-group-stateful); rephrase so that the display reads as part of the sentence.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: give the instance a role, and let admins in through Session Manager. The thing to watch is the role policy that Session Manager needs.
plan.stop_and_answer: An admin can open a Session Manager session to instance A but not to instance B. Neither security group has an inbound rule. Instance B has no instance profile. Why does B fail? Answer: Session Manager needs an instance role with [AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore] (ec2-session-manager-prereq-iam-role); the missing inbound rule is not the problem ([without the need to open inbound ports], ec2-session-manager-no-inbound-ports-bastion-keys).

sections.heading: Instances in several Availability Zones survive the failure of one zone

plan.problem: One instance lives in one place. A fire, a flood or a power fault in that place stops it, whatever its size.
trace: **Choose a Region.** A Region is [a separate geographic area where AWS has multiple Availability Zones] (global-infrastructure-region-is-separate-geographic-area), and [Regions are isolated from each other] (ec2-regions-isolated-not-replicated). Prices differ: [Resource pricing may be different in each Region] (ec2-wa-region-pricing-differs).
**Land in a subnet.** Every instance runs in a subnet, and a subnet [must reside entirely within one Availability Zone] (vpc-subnet-single-az).
**Keep the zones apart.** Each zone runs on [physically distinct, independent infrastructure]; a rare disaster [would only affect a single Availability Zone] (ec2-faq-az-isolation).

**Spread the copies.** Instances [in multiple Availability Zones] protect the application from [the failure of a single location] (ec2-multi-az-protects-from-location-failure); a load balancer or an Auto Scaling group sends work to the zones that still run (chapters 14 and 17, xref).
plan.table: Availability by class of workload (columns: Workload | Placement | Why): production and critical | two or more zones | AWS says to deploy critical components [across multiple Availability Zones] (ec2-bp-multi-az-critical-components); development and test | one zone, stopped outside working hours | you can [save money by deploying your resources in only one Availability Zone] (vpc-dev-test-one-az-saves-money); tiers that exchange much data | a trade-off | traffic [within the same Availability Zone is free], but [charges apply for cross-Availability Zone communication] (ec2-data-transfer-same-az-free-cross-az-charged).
plan.why: Why are zones separate? Common failure points such as generators and cooling are [not shared across Availability Zones] (ec2-faq-az-isolation), so one fault rarely reaches two zones.
plan.exam_signal: "must remain available if an Availability Zone fails" points to instances in two or more zones behind a load balancer or an Auto Scaling group ([in multiple Availability Zones], ec2-multi-az-protects-from-location-failure); "development environment" with "MOST cost-effective" points to one zone (vpc-dev-test-one-az-saves-money).
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence: an AZ ID names [the same physical location in every AWS account] (global-infrastructure-az-id-same-physical-location-every-account); never link the AZ-name fact whose display says 'we'. Local Zones, Wavelength Zones and Outposts belong to chapter 20: one xref clause at most. Distractors may cite trap aws-map-trap-one-az-is-highly-available (chapter 02).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: an instance lives in one zone, so run copies in two or more zones. The thing to watch is the data transfer charge between zones.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team runs two web instances in the same subnet and calls the design highly available. One Availability Zone fails. What happens? Answer: both instances can stop, because a subnet [must reside entirely within one Availability Zone] (vpc-subnet-single-az); the second instance must run in a subnet of another zone.

sections.heading: A placement group decides whether instances sit close together or apart

plan.problem: Some applications need their instances as close as possible, because the instances exchange data all the time. Others need them far apart, so that one hardware fault cannot stop them all.
trace: **Default.** [Placement groups are optional]; without one, EC2 places instances [spread out across the underlying hardware] (ec2-placement-optional-default-spread-out).

**Cluster.** A cluster group keeps instances [within a single Availability Zone] (ec2-placement-cluster-single-az) for [low network latency, high network throughput, or both] when most traffic flows [between the instances in the group] (ec2-placement-cluster-recommended-traffic-between-instances); a single flow reaches [up to 10 Gbps for single-flow traffic] there (ec2-placement-cluster-single-flow-10-gbps).

**Spread.** A spread group puts instances [each placed on distinct hardware], for [a small number of critical instances] (ec2-placement-spread-critical-instances), with at most [seven running instances in each Availability Zone] (ec2-placement-spread-max-7-running-per-az).

**Partition.** In a partition group each partition [has its own set of racks], and no two partitions [share the same racks] (ec2-placement-partition-separate-racks); a group has a [maximum of seven partitions per Availability Zone] (ec2-placement-partition-max-7-per-az) and fits systems [such as HDFS, HBase, and Cassandra] (ec2-placement-partition-distributed-workloads).
plan.table: Three strategies (columns: Group | Instances sit | Limit | Fits): Cluster | close together in one zone | it [can't span multiple Availability Zones] (ec2-placement-cluster-single-az) | tightly coupled HPC; Spread | each on distinct hardware | [seven running instances in each Availability Zone] | a few critical instances; Partition | in groups of racks | [maximum of seven partitions per Availability Zone] | large distributed and replicated systems.
plan.why: Why choose between close and apart? Close hardware cuts latency but shares a fault; separate racks keep a fault small. A partition group helps [isolate the impact of hardware failure] (ec2-placement-partition-separate-racks).
plan.exam_signal: "low latency", "high throughput between nodes" or "tightly coupled HPC" points to a cluster group (ec2-placement-cluster-recommended-traffic-between-instances); "critical instances must not share hardware" points to spread (ec2-placement-spread-critical-instances); "HDFS, HBase or Cassandra" points to partition (ec2-placement-partition-distributed-workloads).
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: placement group rules. An instance is in [one placement group at a time], and [You can't merge placement groups.] (ec2-placement-one-group-per-instance). To move an instance, [the instance must be in the `stopped` state] (ec2-placement-change-requires-stopped). For a cluster group, [Use a single launch request] and [Use the same instance type], or you risk [getting an insufficient capacity error] (ec2-placement-cluster-one-request-one-type). An Elastic Fabric Adapter adds lower latency: it [bypasses the operating system kernel] (ec2-efa-os-bypass). At most 90 words.
plan.spot_the_bug: Spot the bug prompt: a team runs its primary database and two replicas in one cluster placement group 'so that a hardware fault cannot take them all down'. Find the bug. Reveal: a cluster group keeps instances close, [within a single Availability Zone] (ec2-placement-cluster-single-az); for critical instances that must not fail together, a spread group [reduces the risk of simultaneous failures] (ec2-placement-spread-critical-instances). About 65 words with the reveal.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: cluster for speed between nodes, spread or partition to keep failures apart. The thing to watch is that a cluster group stays in one zone.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team needs 12 critical instances in one Availability Zone, each on different hardware. A launch into one spread placement group fails. What fixes it? Answer: a spread group allows [seven running instances in each Availability Zone] (ec2-placement-spread-max-7-running-per-az); AWS recommends you [use multiple spread placement groups] (ec2-placement-spread-more-than-7-use-multiple-groups). The 12 instances are an example value in the prompt.

sections.heading: Stop, reboot and terminate keep different parts of an instance

plan.problem: Stop, reboot and terminate all look like 'turn it off'. Each one keeps a different part of the instance, and exam questions ask which part survives.
trace: **Reboot.** A reboot is [equivalent to rebooting an operating system]: [The instance remains on the same host computer] and keeps [any data on its instance store volumes] (ec2-reboot-same-host-keeps-data).

**Stop.** A stopped instance is not billed for instance usage and [The instance can be started at any time] (ec2-state-stopped-not-billed); [Charges are incurred for the storage] of its EBS volumes (ec2-stopped-instance-type-change).

**Start.** The instance is usually [moved to a new host computer], so [you lose any data on the instance store] (ec2-stop-start-moves-host-loses-instance-store); [The instance gets a new public IPv4 address] (ec2-state-diff-public-ipv4), and it [keeps its private IPv4 address] (ec2-state-diff-private-ipv4).

**Terminate.** [You can't connect to or recover] a terminated instance (ec2-terminated-instance-cannot-recover); its root volume is [deleted by default] (ec2-state-diff-root-volume) through the [DeleteOnTermination] attribute (ec2-delete-on-termination-defaults).
plan.table: Truth table (columns: Part | Reboot | Stop, then start | Terminate): instance store data | [The data is preserved] | [The data is erased] | erased (ec2-state-diff-instance-store-data); public IPv4 address | kept | a new one (ec2-state-diff-public-ipv4) | released; Elastic IP address | [remains associated with the instance] | stays | disassociated (ec2-state-diff-elastic-ip); root EBS volume | kept | kept | [deleted by default] (ec2-state-diff-root-volume); instance usage billed | yes | not while stopped (ec2-state-stopped-not-billed) | no. Hibernation has its own subsection; do not add a column for it.
plan.why: Why does a stop lose the instance store? The instance store is a disk of the old host, and a start usually runs the instance on a [moved to a new host computer] (ec2-stop-start-moves-host-loses-instance-store); rephrase so that the display reads as part of the sentence.
plan.exam_signal: "the data must survive a stop" points to an EBS volume, not the instance store ([The data is erased], ec2-state-diff-instance-store-data); "keep the same public IP address after a stop" points to an Elastic IP address ([remains associated with the instance], ec2-state-diff-elastic-ip).
plan.diagram: Embed ec2-lifecycle after the table (alt and caption count toward the subsection words).
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence each: the instance store fits [temporary storage of information that changes frequently] (instance-store-ideal-for-temporary-data; chapter 22 owns the instance store, xref); termination protection blocks a terminate [using the console, CLI, or API] (ec2-termination-protection-blocks-api) but [does not prevent Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling] (ec2-termination-protection-default-off-not-asg).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: a reboot keeps everything, a stop keeps the volumes, and terminate keeps nothing by default. The thing to watch is the public IP address.
plan.stop_and_answer: A worker keeps temporary files on an instance store volume and its results on an EBS data volume. The team stops the worker overnight to save money. What is left in the morning? Answer: the EBS volume with the results; a stop erases the instance store: [The data is erased] (ec2-state-diff-instance-store-data), and an added EBS volume is kept (ec2-state-diff-root-volume covers the root volume; the data volume survives a stop like every attached EBS volume: link ec2-ebs-root-can-stop-and-restart [can be stopped and later restarted] if the writer needs a link).

sections.heading: Hibernation saves the memory to an encrypted EBS root volume

plan.problem: Some applications take a long time to start: they load data or warm caches into memory. A normal stop throws that memory away, and the next start waits again.
trace: **Turn it on at launch.** You enable hibernation [when you launch it]; you [can't enable hibernation on an existing instance] (ec2-hibernate-enable-only-at-launch). The root volume must be an [EBS volume] and [must be encrypted] (ec2-hibernate-root-volume-requirements).

**Hibernate.** You call the [StopInstances API with an additional ‘Hibernate’ parameter] (ec2-faq-hibernate-trigger-stopinstances); the operating system [saves the contents from the instance memory (RAM)] to the EBS root volume (ec2-hibernate-saves-ram-to-root-volume).

**Wait.** [Hibernated instances are in ‘Stopped’ state] (ec2-faq-hibernated-state-is-stopped); you pay EBS storage, and [you do not incur instance usage fees] (ec2-hibernate-no-instance-fee-ebs-rates).
**Resume.** On start, [the RAM contents are reloaded] and [the instance retains its instance ID] (ec2-hibernate-saves-ram-to-root-volume), so the processes continue where they stopped.
plan.table: Before you count on hibernation (columns: Check | Requirement): root volume | an encrypted EBS volume (ec2-hibernate-root-volume-requirements); memory | Linux at most [150 GiB], Windows at most [16 GiB] (ec2-hibernate-ram-limits-linux-windows); time | at most [60 days] hibernated (ec2-hibernate-max-duration); instance family | a supported family; [bare metal instances are not supported] (ec2-hibernate-supported-families-no-bare-metal); Auto Scaling group | [You can't hibernate an instance] in an [Auto Scaling group or used by Amazon ECS] (ec2-hibernate-not-in-auto-scaling-group).
plan.why: Why must the root volume be encrypted? Memory can hold secrets, and [RAM data is always encrypted] when it moves to the volume (ec2-faq-hibernate-ram-always-encrypted).
plan.exam_signal: "keep the in-memory state", "pre-warmed" or an application that takes a long time to start points to hibernation ([take a long time to bootstrap], ec2-faq-hibernate-use-case-prewarm); "in an Auto Scaling group" points to a warm pool that can [save the contents of your RAM] (ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pool-hibernated-ram; chapter 17, xref).
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence: you cannot change a hibernated instance: [instance is hibernated, you can't modify it] (ec2-hibernate-cannot-modify-while-hibernated); and if the root volume lacks space, [hibernation will fail] and [the instance will get shut down instead] (ec2-faq-hibernate-root-too-small-shuts-down). Spot Instances can hibernate too: subsection 13 (ec2-faq-spot-hibernate-benefit-ram-state).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: hibernation keeps the memory, so a slow application resumes warm. The thing to watch is that you turn it on at launch.
plan.stop_and_answer: A Linux instance has 192 GiB of RAM, an encrypted gp3 root volume, and hibernation turned on at launch. It must keep its memory overnight. Will hibernation work? Answer: no; a Linux instance with more than [150 GiB] of RAM cannot hibernate (ec2-hibernate-ram-limits-linux-windows). The 192 GiB is an example value in the prompt.

sections.heading: Scaling up needs a stop, and scaling out adds instances instead

plan.problem: An instance is too small at the peak, or too big all day. You can make the instance bigger or smaller, or add and remove instances. The two ways behave very differently.
trace: **Measure.** AWS Compute Optimizer reads [existing instance specifications and utilization metrics] and suggests changes to [improve performance, save money, or both] (ec2-compute-optimizer-improve-performance-save-money); an instance is over-provisioned when it can be [sized down while still meeting the performance requirements] (ec2-compute-optimizer-over-provisioned-definition). [you must first opt in to Compute Optimizer] (ec2-compute-optimizer-opt-in-required).
**Stop.** [You must stop your instance] [before you can change its instance type], so you [plan for downtime] (ec2-resize-must-stop-instance).

**Change the type.** The new type needs [the same processor architecture] (ec2-resize-same-processor-architecture), and the change works [only if the instance's current configuration is compatible] (ec2-resize-requires-compatible-configuration).

**Start, or scale out instead.** After the start the instance has [a new public IPv4 address] unless it has an Elastic IP address (ec2-resize-moves-hardware-new-public-ipv4). Scaling out means [adding more instances to handle the load] (ec2-compute-guide-vertical-vs-horizontal-definition); for changing demand, [Horizontal scalability is essential] (ec2-compute-guide-horizontal-for-fluctuating).
plan.table: Two ways to grow (columns: Question | Scale up (vertical) | Scale out (horizontal)): what changes | the size: [increasing the CPU or memory of an instance] | the count: more instances (ec2-compute-guide-vertical-vs-horizontal-definition); downtime | a stop: [You must stop your instance] (ec2-resize-must-stop-instance) | none for the running instances; single point of failure | still one instance | removed when the instances run in several zones (subsection 6).
plan.why: Why measure first? [Over-provisioning cloud resources can lead to extra costs], and [under-provisioning can result in poor performance] (ec2-wa-over-under-provisioning-effects). [Oversized instances waste money] under any purchasing option (ec2-right-size-before-committing).
plan.exam_signal: "over-provisioned" or "low utilization" with "reduce cost" points to right-sizing with Compute Optimizer ([improve performance, save money, or both], ec2-compute-optimizer-improve-performance-save-money); "fluctuating demand" with "no downtime" points to scaling out with an Auto Scaling group (chapter 17), not to a larger instance ([Horizontal scalability is essential], ec2-compute-guide-horizontal-for-fluctuating).
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence: an instance with an instance store root volume cannot be resized in place; the table says [Migrate to a new instance type] (ec2-resize-instance-store-root-migrate). Do not rank vertical against horizontal scaling beyond the two facts above (brief.v0 demand note on vertical and horizontal scaling: the performance pillar does not rank them).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: a bigger instance needs a stop, and more instances need no stop. The thing to watch is that one bigger instance is still one point of failure.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team stops an x86 instance and wants to start it as a Graviton type to save money, with the same AMI. Will that work? Answer: no; the new type needs [the same processor architecture], because [AMIs are specific to the architecture] (ec2-resize-same-processor-architecture); build an arm64 AMI and launch a new instance.

sections.heading: Recovery and a moved network interface keep an instance's addresses after a failure

plan.problem: A single instance fails. Clients, firewall rules and partners know its IP address. The fix must bring the service back at the same address.
trace: **Detect.** EC2 status checks are [performed every minute] (ec2-status-checks-every-minute). A system check finds problems that [require AWS involvement to repair] (ec2-status-check-system-needs-aws); an instance check finds problems that [require your involvement to repair] (ec2-status-check-instance-needs-you).

**Recover in place.** After a failed system check, [simplified automatic recovery is enabled during instance launch] (ec2-recovery-simplified-enabled-by-default) and brings the instance back [including the instance ID], its [private IP addresses, Elastic IP addresses] and [all instance metadata] (ec2-recovery-keeps-id-ips-metadata); [volatile memory (RAM) will be lost] (ec2-recovery-loses-ram-and-cw-instance-store).

**Or move to a standby.** Detach a secondary network interface and attach it to a [hot standby instance]: the interface [maintains its private IP addresses, Elastic IP addresses] and its MAC address, with [no changes to the route table] (ec2-eni-hot-standby-failover). It attaches only to instances [in the same Availability Zone] (ec2-eni-attributes-follow-same-az).
**Or remap an address.** An Elastic IP address is [a static IPv4 address]; you can mask a failure by [rapidly remapping the address to another instance] (ec2-eip-mask-instance-failure-remap).
plan.table: Which repair keeps what (columns: Failure | Who repairs | What you do | What stays): system check fails (host problem) | AWS | automatic recovery, or a stop and start (ec2-stop-start-fix-for-failed-status-check) | instance ID, private IP, Elastic IP; instance check fails (your software) | you | a reboot alarm action, [recommended for Instance Health Check failures] (ec2-alarm-reboot-instance-check-recover-system-check) | everything on EBS; the instance is lost | you | move the secondary interface or the Elastic IP address to a standby | the address.
plan.why: Why can a moved interface keep its addresses? The addresses belong to the interface, not to the instance: [The attributes of a network interface follow it] (ec2-eni-attributes-follow-same-az).
plan.exam_signal: "a secondary network interface" with "fail over to a standby instance" points to moving the interface in the same zone (ec2-eni-hot-standby-failover); "the same instance ID and IP address after a hardware failure" points to automatic recovery (ec2-recovery-keeps-id-ips-metadata); "replace failed instances automatically" points to an Auto Scaling group, because moving an interface or an Elastic IP address by hand is the [attach a network interface or Elastic IP address] option for a basic failover (ec2-bp-basic-failover-eni-or-eip).
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: scheduled events and recovery limits. AWS can [schedule events to reboot, stop, and retire] instances, and [AWS notifies you in advance by email] (ec2-scheduled-events-reboot-stop-retire). After [irreparable failure of the underlying host], an instance with an EBS root volume [the instance is scheduled to stop]; one with an instance store root volume [the instance is scheduled to terminate] (ec2-retirement-ebs-stop-instance-store-terminate). Simplified recovery is [Not supported for instances that attach instance store] (ec2-recovery-simplified-not-instance-store). At most 90 words.
plan.body_extras: The primary interface cannot move: [You can't detach a primary network interface] (ec2-eni-primary-cannot-detach); say it in one clause of step 3 if words allow. Application status checks (2026-08-10) are not examinable yet: they appear only in the entry under the B-list.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: recovery brings back the same instance, and a moved interface brings back the same address. The thing to watch is the zone: an interface moves only inside it.
plan.stop_and_answer: After a bad kernel update, an instance fails its instance status check. The team waits for automatic recovery. Does recovery start? Answer: no; recovery acts when an instance [fails a system status check], not [if only the instance status check fails] (ec2-recovery-system-status-check-only); the team repairs it, for example with the reboot alarm action (ec2-alarm-reboot-instance-check-recover-system-check).

sections.heading: On-Demand bills each second, and a commitment lowers the price of steady use

plan.problem: On-Demand is simple: you pay for what runs. For servers that run all year, that simplicity costs money, and AWS lowers the price if you commit.
trace: **Pay as you go.** On-Demand Instances are billed for the seconds they run, with a [60-second minimum] (ec2-on-demand-billing-per-second-60s-minimum); AWS recommends them for [short-term, irregular workloads that cannot be interrupted] (ec2-on-demand-recommended-short-term-irregular).

**Commit to a spend.** A Savings Plan is [a commitment to a consistent amount of usage, in USD per hour, for a term of 1 or 3 years] (ec2-purchasing-options-list). Steady-state workloads [benefit most from long-term commitments through Savings Plans] (ec2-steady-state-savings-plans).

**Choose the flexibility.** Compute Savings Plans apply [regardless of Region, instance family, operating system] and [also cover Fargate and Lambda usage]; EC2 Instance Savings Plans cover [a specific instance family within a Region] (ec2-savings-plans-two-ec2-types-flexibility), for [up to 72%] against [up to 66%] (ec2-savings-plans-vs-ri-discounts-66-72).

**Or reserve a configuration.** [Reserved Instances are not physical instances]: an RI is a billing discount on matching instances (ec2-ri-is-billing-discount-not-instance), and AWS now says it would [generally recommend replacing with Savings Plans] (ec2-reserved-instances-older-option-savings-plans-recommended).
plan.table: Three ways to pay for the same instance (columns: Question | On-Demand | Compute Savings Plan | EC2 Instance Savings Plan): commitment | none | USD per hour for 1 or 3 years | the same, for one family in one Region; discount | none | [up to 66%] | [up to 72%] (ec2-savings-plans-vs-ri-discounts-66-72); follows a move to another Region | yes | yes: [Compute Savings Plans apply across all Regions] (ec2-compute-sp-discount-follows-regions) | no: [scoped to a specific Region]; fits | short or unknown use | steady use that may change shape | steady use of one family.
plan.why: Why match the price to the part? The cost pillar puts resources that run for [extended periods (for commitment discounts)] and ones that are [dynamic and short-running (for spot or on-demand)] (ec2-wa-pricing-model-per-component).
plan.exam_signal: "steady-state", "predictable" or "for the next 3 years" points to a Savings Plan ([benefit most from long-term commitments through Savings Plans], ec2-steady-state-savings-plans); "may change instance family or Region" or "also AWS Fargate" points to a Compute Savings Plan (ec2-savings-plans-two-ec2-types-flexibility); "sandbox" or "used only in working hours" points to On-Demand and turning instances off ([you might choose an on-demand model], ec2-wa-sandbox-on-demand-environments-savings-plans; [70% or more] saved, ec2-wa-turn-off-after-hours-70-percent).
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: Reserved Instance details. A Standard RI gives [the most significant discount], and [Standard Reserved Instances can't be exchanged]; a Convertible RI [can be exchanged for another Convertible Reserved Instance] (ec2-ri-standard-biggest-discount-modify-only). A regional RI applies [in any Availability Zone in the specified Region] (ec2-ri-az-flexibility). RIs [do not renew automatically] (ec2-ri-no-automatic-renewal), and you [cannot cancel your purchase] (ec2-ri-purchase-cannot-be-cancelled). Discounts apply in this order: [Reserved Instances first, then Amazon EC2 Instance Savings Plans, then Compute Savings Plans] (ec2-commitment-discount-application-order). At most 90 words: drop the order sentence first if over.
plan.body_extras: Do not teach Savings Plans types beyond the two EC2 ones; chapter 41 owns Savings Plans and Database Savings Plans (xref). Never state a price.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: pay On-Demand for what changes, and commit for what runs all year. The thing to watch is that a commitment is a discount, not a server.
plan.stop_and_answer: A company runs 20 steady instances in one Region and plans to move half of the work to AWS Fargate next year. Which commitment keeps its discount after the move? Answer: a Compute Savings Plan, because Compute Savings Plans [also cover Fargate and Lambda usage]; an EC2 Instance Savings Plan covers only [a specific instance family within a Region] (ec2-savings-plans-two-ec2-types-flexibility). The 20 instances are an example value.

sections.heading: Spot Instances use spare capacity that EC2 can take back with two minutes notice

plan.problem: AWS has idle capacity in every Availability Zone. It sells that capacity cheaply on one condition: it can take the capacity back when it needs it.
trace: **Request spare capacity.** With Spot you [Request unused EC2 instances] (ec2-purchasing-options-list) at [up to 90%] off the On-Demand price (ec2-spot-discount-up-to-90-percent). The price is [set by Amazon EC2, and is adjusted gradually based on the long-term supply of and demand] (ec2-spot-price-set-by-ec2-not-bid).
**Run like any instance.** While it runs, a Spot Instance is [exactly the same as On-Demand or Reserved instances] (ec2-faq-spot-same-instances-as-on-demand).

**Get the warning.** When EC2 needs the capacity back, you get [two minutes of notice] (ec2-spot-only-difference-interruption-two-minutes), [as an EventBridge event] and [as items in the instance metadata] (ec2-spot-interruption-notice-channels).

**Lose the instance.** EC2 [terminates the instance by default] (ec2-spot-interruption-default-terminate); to stop or hibernate it instead, [The Spot Instance request type must be persistent] (ec2-spot-stop-behavior-needs-persistent-request).
plan.table: Does the work fit Spot? (columns: Workload | Spot? | Why): stateless web servers, CI/CD, big data, rendering | yes | AWS recommends Spot for [stateless, fault-tolerant, flexible applications] (ec2-spot-recommended-stateless-fault-tolerant-flexible); background batch that can wait | yes | [Spot Instances offer significant cost savings] (ec2-batch-delayable-workloads-spot); a database, or a job that must finish by a deadline | no | Spot is not for work that is [inflexible, stateful, fault-intolerant, or tightly coupled] (ec2-spot-not-suitable-stateful-inflexible).
plan.why: Why is it so cheap? You buy capacity that would otherwise sit idle, without a promise to keep it: [Spot does not guarantee] that instances run long enough to finish (ec2-spot-no-guarantee-to-finish).
plan.exam_signal: "can tolerate interruptions", "can restart" or "fault-tolerant batch" with MOST cost-effective points to Spot ([can tolerate interruptions], ec2-spot-vs-savings-plans-guideline); "cannot be interrupted" or "must finish by" points to On-Demand or a commitment (ec2-on-demand-recommended-short-term-irregular); "reduce Spot interruptions" points to many instance types and zones with the price-capacity-optimized strategy ([the most-available Spot capacity pools], ec2-spot-price-capacity-optimized-recommended).
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: requests, prices and fleets. A persistent request [remains active until it expires] and opens again after an interruption (ec2-spot-persistent-request-resubmitted). You pay the Spot price, [not your maximum price] (ec2-spot-max-price-default-on-demand-pay-spot-price), and setting a maximum price gets instances [interrupted more frequently] (ec2-spot-max-price-more-interruptions). If EC2 interrupts in the first hour, there is [No charge] (ec2-spot-interrupted-by-aws-first-hour-free). Be flexible across [at least 10 instance types] (ec2-spot-rule-of-thumb-10-instance-types). At most 90 words.
plan.body_extras: Only if words remain, one sentence: a fleet does not fall back to On-Demand; it will [attempt to meet your desired Spot capacity] (ec2-faq-fleet-no-on-demand-failover). Never say 'bid': the Spot price is set by EC2. Do not let the 2022-11 change date decide an answer; the current recommendation is price-capacity-optimized.

sections.heading: Only a reservation holds capacity, and a Dedicated Host holds a whole server

plan.problem: Two promises are easy to mix up. A discount lowers the price, but it keeps no server free for you. And default hardware is shared with other accounts, which some licenses and rules do not allow.
trace: **Separate price and capacity.** Purchasing options [determine how AWS calculates your bill]; Capacity Reservations [determine whether capacity is held for you] (ec2-purchasing-vs-capacity-reservation-independent).

**Hold capacity in one zone.** An On-Demand Capacity Reservation holds capacity [in a specific Availability Zone for any duration], and [there is no term commitment] (ec2-capacity-reservation-immediate-no-term). It is [charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate] whether you use it or not (ec2-capacity-reservation-charged-used-or-not), and [Savings Plans and Regional Reserved Instances apply] to lower that rate (ec2-capacity-reservation-discount-from-sp-or-regional-ri).

**Isolate the hardware.** By default instances [run on shared tenancy hardware] (ec2-default-tenancy-shared-hardware); Dedicated Instances run on [hardware that's dedicated to a single AWS account] (ec2-dedicated-instance-isolated-from-other-accounts).

**Own the whole server.** A Dedicated Host is [a physical server that is fully dedicated] to you (ec2-dedicated-host-physical-server); it shows [the number of sockets and physical cores] (ec2-dedicated-host-socket-core-visibility), so you can bring [per-socket, per-core, or per-VM software licenses] (ec2-dedicated-host-byol-per-socket-core).

traps.belief: Buying a Savings Plan or a Reserved Instance makes AWS keep capacity free for your instances.
traps.truth: Savings Plans do not provide a capacity reservation, and a regional Reserved Instance does not reserve capacity. Only a zonal Reserved Instance or an On-Demand Capacity Reservation holds capacity, in one Availability Zone.

traps.belief: Spot is the cheapest option, so it is right for any cost-sensitive job, also one that must not be interrupted.
traps.truth: Amazon EC2 can interrupt a Spot Instance with two minutes of notice, and Spot does not suit inflexible or fault-intolerant work. AWS recommends On-Demand for short-term, irregular workloads that cannot be interrupted.

traps.belief: An instance keeps its public IPv4 address when it is stopped and started again.
traps.truth: After a stop and start the instance gets a new public IPv4 address; it keeps its private IPv4 address, and an Elastic IP address stays associated.

traps.belief: You can hibernate any running instance whenever you want to keep its memory.
traps.truth: Hibernation must be turned on when the instance is launched, the root volume must be an encrypted EBS volume, the RAM must fit the limit (Linux 150 GiB, Windows 16 GiB), and the family must support it.

traps.belief: A Dedicated Instance is enough for software licenses that count sockets or physical cores.
traps.truth: Only a Dedicated Host shows the number of sockets and physical cores and supports per-socket and per-core licenses; Dedicated Instances give no such visibility and no control over placement.

traps.belief: Any job can move to AWS Lambda to avoid managing servers.
traps.truth: A Lambda function runs for at most 15 minutes. Long or persistent processes fit AWS Fargate, AWS Batch or EC2.

traps.belief: A burstable T instance can run at high CPU all day for its normal hourly price.
traps.truth: A T instance earns credits below its baseline and spends them above it. In unlimited mode, an average above the baseline over 24 hours adds a charge per vCPU-hour; for steady high CPU, AWS suggests M or C instances.

traps.belief: An AMI can launch instances in any Region.
traps.truth: AMIs are Region-specific resources. To launch in another Region you copy the AMI there first, and the copy does not take the launch permissions with it.

traps.belief: To manage instances in a private subnet, you need a bastion host and an open SSH port.
traps.truth: Session Manager gives a shell without inbound ports, bastion hosts or SSH keys, when the instance role has AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore. EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint reaches instances without a bastion and without a public IP address.

traps.belief: A cluster placement group makes an application highly available.
traps.truth: A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one Availability Zone for low latency and high throughput. To keep critical instances on distinct hardware, use a spread placement group.

traps.belief: Stopping an instance keeps the data on its instance store volumes, as a reboot does.
traps.truth: A reboot keeps instance store data; a stop, a hibernation and a termination erase it. Data that must survive belongs on EBS.

traps.belief: You can change the instance type of a running instance with no downtime.
traps.truth: You must stop an EBS-backed instance before you change its type, so you plan for downtime. To add capacity without stopping anything, scale out with more instances.

traps.belief: You can move a network interface to a standby instance in another Availability Zone.
traps.truth: A network interface attaches only to instances in its own Availability Zone. Its private IP addresses, Elastic IP addresses and MAC address move with it to a standby in that zone.

traps.belief: A stopped instance keeps its memory and continues where it left off when it starts again.
traps.truth: A stop clears the RAM. Only hibernation saves the RAM to the encrypted EBS root volume and reloads it at the next start.
traps.note: added by questions-16-2 for distractor tagging (Q205); used in questions only, not planned as a callout

traps.belief: A higher maximum Spot price protects Spot Instances from interruption.
traps.truth: Amazon EC2 sets the Spot price from long-term supply and demand, and instances with a maximum price are interrupted more frequently than without one. Flexibility across instance types and Availability Zones lowers interruptions.

faq.q: Does a Savings Plan reserve capacity for your instances?
faq.answer: No; reserve it with an On-Demand Capacity Reservation, which a Savings Plan can make cheaper

faq.q: Does a Reserved Instance discount apply to Spot Instances or to instances on a Dedicated Host?
faq.answer: No; Dedicated Hosts have their own reservations

faq.answer: No; its Region is fixed for the whole term

faq.q: Does an EC2 Fleet switch to On-Demand Instances when Spot capacity runs short?
faq.answer: No; it keeps trying to get Spot capacity

faq.answer: No; Amazon EC2 resumes it when capacity returns

question_slots.twin: first of strict twin pair A (twin q06)
question_slots.note: Shared stem: a company runs a data processing job every night on EC2 instances; the job takes about 3 hours; MOST cost-effective. Changed phrase: 'The job must not be interrupted, and it must finish before the business day starts.' Key: (B) On-Demand Instances ([short-term, irregular workloads that cannot be interrupted], ec2-on-demand-recommended-short-term-irregular). Options identical in q06: (A) Spot Instances (trap ec2-trap-spot-for-uninterruptible in q01; why links ec2-spot-only-difference-interruption-two-minutes and ec2-spot-not-suitable-stateful-inflexible); (B) On-Demand Instances; (C) Standard Reserved Instances for 3 years with All Upfront payment, for instances that run 3 hours a day (violates-qualifier: a term commitment for a part-time job, ec2-ri-term-one-or-three-years); (D) Dedicated Hosts (misconception: they solve licensing, not cost, ec2-purchasing-option-guidance). Do not offer a Savings Plan option: its hourly-commitment math would make the key arguable. Official sample question type: On-Demand for jobs that must not be interrupted.

question_slots.twin: first of strict twin pair B (twin q09)
question_slots.note: Shared stem: a company runs 8 instances of one type for a mission-critical application in one Region; which purchasing approach meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively? Changed phrase: 'The company must ensure that capacity for all 8 instances is always available in one specific Availability Zone.' Key: (A) an On-Demand Capacity Reservation in that Availability Zone ([in a specific Availability Zone for any duration], ec2-capacity-reservation-immediate-no-term; ec2-faq-capacity-reservation-strict-requirements). Options identical in q09: (A) an On-Demand Capacity Reservation in that Availability Zone; (B) a Compute Savings Plan (trap ec2-trap-reservation-holds-capacity; why links ec2-faq-savings-plans-no-capacity-reservation); (C) an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for that instance family in the Region (trap ec2-trap-reservation-holds-capacity in q02); (D) Spot Instances with the capacity-optimized allocation strategy (misconception: Spot can be interrupted, ec2-spot-only-difference-interruption-two-minutes).

question_slots.twin: first of strict twin pair C (twin q12)
question_slots.note: Shared stem: a company launches 6 EC2 instances of one type in one Availability Zone for a new application. Changed phrase: 'The instances exchange data constantly and need the lowest possible network latency between them.' Key: (A) a cluster placement group (ec2-placement-cluster-recommended-traffic-between-instances). Options identical in q12: (A) a cluster placement group; (B) a spread placement group (misconception in q03: distinct hardware does not lower latency, ec2-placement-spread-critical-instances); (C) a partition placement group with one instance in each partition (misconception, ec2-placement-partition-separate-racks); (D) no placement group, because EC2 already spreads instances out (misconception; why links ec2-placement-optional-default-spread-out). qualifier may be 'none' (difficulty 1); state the stem so that exactly one option is right.

A reporting application on two Linux instances loads its data into memory for 20 minutes at every start. The instances run only in business hours. They were launched from a launch template with hibernation enabled, an encrypted EBS root volume large enough for the RAM, and 64 GiB of RAM (state all prerequisites so that the key is clear; they are not in an Auto Scaling group). The company wants to avoid the 20-minute load each morning and pay as little as possible at night, with the LEAST operational overhead. Key: hibernate the instances each evening and start them each morning (ec2-faq-hibernate-use-case-prewarm, ec2-hibernate-saves-ram-to-root-volume, ec2-hibernate-no-instance-fee-ebs-rates). Distractors: stop and start them normally (misconception: [RAM is cleared], ec2-faq-hibernate-vs-stop-ram); keep the data cache on instance store volumes and stop the instances (trap ec2-trap-stop-keeps-instance-store); keep them running all night with Reserved Instances (violates-qualifier: cost). The slot trap ec2-trap-hibernate-any-instance goes on a distractor only if one states it exactly; otherwise the trap stays on q16.

A licensed application runs on one EC2 instance; partners allow-list its private IP address and the license is bound to its MAC address. A hot standby instance runs in the same Availability Zone. On failure, traffic must move to the standby with minimal downtime and no DNS or route table changes. Key: put the address on a secondary network interface and move that interface to the standby (ec2-eni-hot-standby-failover, ec2-eni-attributes-follow-same-az). Distractors: move the interface to a standby in another Availability Zone (trap ec2-trap-eni-across-az); detach the primary network interface and attach it to the standby (impossible-feature; why links ec2-eni-primary-cannot-detach); stop and start the failed instance, because it keeps its public IP address (trap ec2-trap-stop-keeps-public-ip; why links ec2-state-diff-public-ipv4). Official sample question type: secondary network interface for failover.

question_slots.twin: twin_of q01 (strict: the same stem and options; only the requirement phrase changes)
question_slots.note: Changed phrase: 'The job can tolerate interruptions: it restarts from its last checkpoint, and it may finish later in the day.' Key: (A) Spot Instances ([stateless, fault-tolerant, flexible applications], ec2-spot-recommended-stateless-fault-tolerant-flexible; [up to 90%], ec2-spot-discount-up-to-90-percent). Option B fails as violates-qualifier (On-Demand costs more); C violates-qualifier; D misconception. Bullet also 4.2.K4.

An analytics service keeps a large data set in memory and runs out of memory while CPU use stays low. Which instance family meets these requirements? Key: memory optimized (R) (ec2-family-memory-optimized, ec2-instance-type-series-letters). Distractors: compute optimized C (misconception: pays for CPU, ec2-family-compute-optimized); burstable T (misconception: credits help CPU, not memory, ec2-burstable-standard-earn-spend-credits); storage optimized I (misconception: local disk I/O, ec2-family-storage-optimized). Bullet also 4.2.K7.

A web application on one large general purpose instance averages 9% CPU use, with short peaks to 85% on weekday mornings (Callvale's numbers, no name). MOST cost-effective change that still serves the peaks. Key: a smaller burstable T instance (ec2-burstable-low-utilization-waste-use-t, ec2-burstable-standard-earn-spend-credits, ec2-compute-optimizer-over-provisioned-definition). Distractors: a larger compute optimized instance (violates-qualifier); keep the size and buy a 3-year Reserved Instance (trap how-the-exam-asks-trap-cheapest-wins is not exact: use misconception 'a discount on an oversized instance', ec2-right-size-before-committing); a memory optimized instance (misconception). Think-aloud: find the constraint (low average, short peaks), predict T, check credits cover the peak. Bullet also 4.2.K7.

Changed phrase: 'The instances run all day for the next 3 years in a steady state; the company will not change instance family or Region, and capacity is not a concern.' Key: (C) an EC2 Instance Savings Plan ([up to 72%] against [up to 66%], ec2-savings-plans-vs-ri-discounts-66-72; ec2-savings-plans-two-ec2-types-flexibility). Option A fails as violates-qualifier (charged at the On-Demand rate, ec2-capacity-reservation-charged-used-or-not); B fails as violates-qualifier (lower discount); D misconception (steady work, interruptions). Bullet also 4.2.S3.

A containerized job runs once a day for 40 to 90 minutes. The team does not want to manage servers. Select TWO compute options that meet these requirements. Keys: AWS Fargate (ec2-compute-guide-fargate-no-servers-for-containers, lambda-choose-fargate-containers-persistent); AWS Batch on Fargate resources (ec2-neighbour-batch-runs-on-ec2-fargate, ec2-neighbour-batch-provisions-for-jobs). Distractors: AWS Lambda (trap ec2-trap-lambda-runs-any-job; why links lambda-faq-timeout-15-minutes); an EC2 instance that runs all day (violates-qualifier: servers to manage, ec2-compute-guide-ec2-overhead-justified-for-control); AWS Elastic Beanstalk (misconception: [specifically designed for running web applications], ec2-compute-guide-beanstalk-web-apps). Bullet also 4.2.S3.

Administrators need shell access to EC2 instances in private subnets; the company wants no inbound ports and no SSH keys. The instances already reach AWS service endpoints (state it, so that network paths do not decide: no fact on the SSM Agent path yet, fr-0061). MOST secure. Select TWO. Keys: attach an instance role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy (ec2-session-manager-prereq-iam-role); remove the inbound SSH rules and connect with Session Manager (ec2-session-manager-no-inbound-ports-bastion-keys, vpc-wa-sec06-no-ssh-rdp-use-session-manager). Distractors: a bastion host in a public subnet with port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0 (trap ec2-trap-ssh-needs-bastion); store an access key on each instance for the agent (trap iam-trap-keys-on-instance); allow port 22 only from the office IP range (violates-qualifier: an open port and keys remain).

Changed phrase: 'The instances are mission-critical, and a single hardware failure must not affect more than one of them.' Key: (B) a spread placement group ([each placed on distinct hardware], ec2-placement-spread-critical-instances; 6 instances fit [seven running instances in each Availability Zone], ec2-placement-spread-max-7-running-per-az). Option A carries trap ec2-trap-cluster-for-ha; C fails because one partition can hold several instances on shared racks (misconception); D fails because the default spreading is a best effort, not a rule (misconception, ec2-placement-optional-default-spread-out).

A company has a production web tier that must stay available if an Availability Zone fails, and a development environment that engineers use only in office hours. Meet both needs MOST cost-effectively. Select TWO. Keys: run the production instances in two or more Availability Zones behind a load balancer (ec2-multi-az-protects-from-location-failure, ec2-bp-multi-az-critical-components); run development in one Availability Zone and stop it outside office hours (vpc-dev-test-one-az-saves-money, ec2-wa-turn-off-after-hours-70-percent, ec2-faq-stopped-instance-ebs-still-charged). Distractors: production on larger instances in one zone (trap aws-map-trap-one-az-is-highly-available); development across three zones with Capacity Reservations (trap how-the-exam-asks-trap-always-max-availability); production active in two Regions (trap aws-map-trap-multi-region-for-high-availability: more than needed). Bullet also 4.2.K3.

A company builds its instances from a custom AMI in us-east-1 and must be able to launch identical instances in us-west-2 for disaster recovery, with the LEAST operational overhead. Key: copy the AMI to us-west-2 and use the copy in a launch template there (ec2-ami-region-specific-copy). Distractors: use the same AMI ID in a us-west-2 launch template (trap ec2-trap-ami-global); add us-west-2 to the AMI's launch permissions (misconception: launch permissions name accounts, organizations or OUs, ec2-ami-launch-permissions-categories); rebuild the instances in us-west-2 by hand from a runbook (violates-qualifier). Bullet also 4.2.K3.

A legacy application runs on one EBS-backed x86 instance and cannot run on more than one instance. It now needs twice the memory. A 30-minute maintenance window is allowed tonight; minimal downtime. Key: in the window, stop the instance, change it to a larger memory optimized x86 type, and start it (ec2-resize-must-stop-instance, ec2-resize-same-processor-architecture, ec2-stopped-instance-type-change). Wrong path in the think-aloud: step 3 predicts 'change the type while it runs'; step 5: 'My first idea breaks because the instance must be stopped before its type changes.' Distractors: change the instance type while it runs (trap ec2-trap-resize-running-instance); add a second instance behind a load balancer (violates-requirement: the application runs on one instance only); change to a Graviton type of the same size class with the same AMI (impossible-feature; why links ec2-resize-same-processor-architecture); hibernate the instance and change its type while it is hibernated (impossible-feature; why links ec2-hibernate-cannot-modify-while-hibernated). Use at most one impossible-feature distractor: pick one of the last two. Bullet also 4.2.K9.

Ten running Linux instances (32 GiB RAM each, not in an Auto Scaling group) were launched without hibernation and with unencrypted root volumes. The company must keep their memory state across nightly stops. Key: create a new launch template version with hibernation enabled and an encrypted EBS root volume large enough for the RAM, then launch replacement instances from it (ec2-hibernate-enable-only-at-launch, ec2-hibernate-root-volume-requirements). Distractors: turn on hibernation for the running instances and stop them with the Hibernate parameter (trap ec2-trap-hibernate-any-instance; impossible-feature, why links ec2-hibernate-enable-only-at-launch); stop them normally each night (misconception: RAM is cleared, ec2-faq-hibernate-vs-stop-ram); put them in an Auto Scaling group and hibernate them there (misconception: ec2-hibernate-not-in-auto-scaling-group). Bullet also 4.2.S2.

A company migrates database servers to EC2 and wants to keep its existing licenses, which count physical cores; the vendor asks for the socket and core count. MOST cost-effective. Key: Dedicated Hosts with the existing licenses (ec2-dedicated-host-byol-per-socket-core, ec2-dedicated-host-socket-core-visibility, ec2-dedicated-host-byol-no-software-charge). Distractors: Dedicated Instances (trap ec2-trap-dedicated-instance-for-byol); shared-tenancy On-Demand Instances with license-included AMIs (violates-requirement: buys new licenses); Spot Instances on default tenancy (misconception).

A batch workload that can tolerate interruptions runs on Spot Instances of one instance type in one Availability Zone, with the lowest-price allocation strategy; interruptions are frequent and jobs restart often. Reduce interruptions and keep costs low with the LEAST operational overhead. Key: an Auto Scaling group with many instance types across several Availability Zones and the price-capacity-optimized strategy (ec2-spot-price-capacity-optimized-recommended, ec2-spot-be-flexible-types-and-azs, ec2-fleet-auto-scaling-recommended-method). Distractors: keep lowest-price because it is the cheapest (trap how-the-exam-asks-trap-cheapest-wins; why links ec2-fleet-spot-price-capacity-optimized-recommended [highest risk of interruption]); set a higher maximum price so that EC2 interrupts less (misconception: [interrupted more frequently], ec2-spot-max-price-more-interruptions; price set by EC2, ec2-spot-price-set-by-ec2-not-bid); an EC2 Fleet that falls back to On-Demand when Spot runs short (impossible-feature; why links ec2-faq-fleet-no-on-demand-failover). Do not let the 2022-11 change date decide the key. Bullet also 4.2.K9.

A T3 instance in unlimited mode runs at about 80% CPU all day; the bill shows extra CPU credit charges every month. MOST cost-effective change. Key: move to an M or C instance with a similar vCPU count (ec2-faq-burstable-sustained-high-cpu-use-m-or-c, ec2-burstable-unlimited-24-hour-baseline-rule). Distractors: keep the T3 instance in unlimited mode, because the hourly price covers all bursts (trap ec2-trap-burstable-for-steady-cpu); switch the T3 instance to standard mode (misconception: performance falls to the baseline when credits run out, ec2-faq-t2-zero-credits-baseline: state the T2 scope or avoid the link); run the T3 workload on Spot in unlimited mode (misconception, ec2-burstable-spot-standard-mode-recommended). Bullet also 4.2.S5.

A single EBS-backed instance (not in an Auto Scaling group, no instance store volumes) must come back automatically after a host hardware failure with the same instance ID, private IP address and Elastic IP address. Key: rely on automatic recovery after a failed system status check, or a CloudWatch alarm with the recover action (ec2-recovery-system-status-check-only, ec2-recovery-keeps-id-ips-metadata, ec2-alarm-reboot-instance-check-recover-system-check). Distractors: a CloudWatch alarm with the reboot action on the system status check (misconception: reboot fits instance check failures, ec2-alarm-reboot-instance-check-recover-system-check); place the instance behind a load balancer, which replaces it when health checks fail (trap elb-trap-lb-replaces-instance); a scheduled job that launches a new instance from the AMI (violates-requirement: a new instance ID).

A nightly analytics cluster of EC2 instances exchanges terabytes between nodes. It can be rebuilt from scratch, and a delay of a day is acceptable if an Availability Zone fails. The data transfer bill is high because the nodes run in three Availability Zones. MOST cost-effective change. Key: run all nodes in one Availability Zone (for example in a cluster placement group) (ec2-data-transfer-same-az-free-cross-az-charged, ec2-faq-cross-az-transfer-charged-both-sides). Distractors: keep three zones for the highest availability (trap how-the-exam-asks-trap-always-max-availability); give each node an Elastic IP address and send traffic to those addresses (misconception: public or Elastic IP addresses also bring regional data transfer rates, ec2-faq-regional-transfer-charged-once); move half the nodes to another Region (misconception: [a charge for data transfer across Regions], ec2-data-transfer-cross-region-charged). Bullet also 4.2.S3.

A company runs a Python web service and a small helper written in C on x86 instances, and wants the better price performance of Graviton with minimal code changes. Which step is required? Key: build an arm64 AMI and recompile the C helper for Arm; the Python code runs with minimal or no changes (ec2-graviton-compiled-apps-recompile, ec2-graviton-40-percent-better-price-performance, ec2-resize-same-processor-architecture). Distractors: stop the instances and change their type to Graviton with the current AMI (impossible-feature; why links ec2-resize-same-processor-architecture); rewrite the Python service in a compiled language (violates-qualifier); turn on nested virtualization to run the x86 build (misconception). ec2-graviton-needs-arm64-ami names only M6g and A1: keep that scope or do not cite it. Bullet also 4.2.K7.
